articles.title: Self-hosted LLM vs API: calculating the breakeven point
articles.excerpt: Renting a server with a single RTX 4090 graphics card costs about $317 a month. API requests for the Llama 3.1 8B model on OpenRouter start from $0.05 per 1 million tokens. A self-hosted server pays o…
articles.body: Renting a server with a single RTX 4090 graphics card costs about $317 a month . API requests for the Llama 3.1 8B model on OpenRouter start from $0.05 per 1 million tokens . A self-hosted server pays off only with continuous 24/7 generation. Any pause in operation makes buying tokens significantly cheaper. Calculating hardware rental costs against buying tokens Developers often view dropping an API provider as direct savings. In practice, renting a bare chip eats up more budget due to the radical drop in token prices over recent years. Provider price wars have pushed inference costs to an absolute minimum. An RTX 4090 server costs $0.44 for every hour of operation. Multiply $0.44 by 24 hours to get $10.56 a day. Multiply that by 30 days to get $316.80 a month. Round it up to $317.
articles.author: Andrey Altrouter

articles.title: Three rows per wish: keeping a free app inside Cloudflare D1's daily limits
articles.excerpt: What one user action costs in rows read and written, and the four changes that cut ours To keep a D1 app cheap, count the rows each user action writes, because D1 bills every index entry an insert tou…
articles.body: What one user action costs in rows read and written, and the four changes that cut ours To keep a D1 app cheap, count the rows each user action writes, because D1 bills every index entry an insert touches as another written row. Then drop indexes that only serve rare queries, keep counters in triggers instead of running COUNT(*) , and answer repeat reads from the edge cache. In Wish Tree, sending a wish went from five rows written to three. This matters more now than it did a few months ago. Since September 1, 2026, D1 queries on the Workers Free plan fail once the account passes the daily limit : 5 million rows read or 100,000 rows written per day, reset at midnight UTC. A busy evening is no longer just a bigger bill. It can be an outage.

articles.title: On Skio, the Swap Button Tells You What the Renewal Could Not
articles.excerpt: Skio stores generate a particular kind of evidence, and most of it sits unread in the subscription portal. When a subscriber swaps a product instead of cancelling, they are saying something precise: t…
articles.body: Skio stores generate a particular kind of evidence, and most of it sits unread in the subscription portal. When a subscriber swaps a product instead of cancelling, they are saying something precise: the relationship is fine, the item is wrong. When they skip a delivery, the message is different again — the cadence, not the product, missed their life. And when they do nothing at all and the renewal simply fails at the card, there is no message, which is exactly the problem worth separating from the other two. That separation is the whole game when reading loss on this platform.

articles.body: I had a perfectly normal Next.js app, and I wanted it running on Cloudflare Workers . That's it. That was the whole plan. Then I found out there are two ways to do it in 2026, and because I can't leave well enough alone, I tried both. Road one is vinext , a Vite -native framework that's compatible with Next. Road two is OpenNext (specifically @opennextjs/cloudflare ), which takes Next's own server output and tucks it inside a Worker. Spoiler: both work. And both are "free" as far as the platform bill goes.
